correctness.rationale: For all a,b>=1 the exact hub-and-leaf update is proved. Leaf synchronization on periodic orbits partitions all recurrent trajectories by which hubs ever turn off. The two-always-on case yields (2^a-2)(2^b-2) period-two states. Exactly one hub always on yields a forced three-step other-hub clock paired with an alternating leaf subset, producing 3[T(a)+T(b)] period-six states. Both hubs ever off forces uniform leaf blocks, exhaustively reduced to sixteen states in four size regimes: one fixed configuration and one three-cycle iff a,b>=2. Two separately implemented finite programs match all counts in the stated ranges; numerical checks are not extrapolated.

value.rationale: Double stars are the first nontrivial two-hub tree family; a complete, unbounded two-parameter classification exposes two independent sharp onset thresholds and a reversal from only six-cycles (besides the fixed point) in thin arms to overwhelming period-two dominance among recurrent states in balanced large arms. It gives explicit labelled orbit numbers, not a routine reparameterization of a known table or single finite experiment.
